attacks.claim: Widths above the source are not clamped. An original or crop smaller than 1200 or 1600 px yields upscaled derivatives, and the srcset still advertises those widths, so browsers pick blurry files.
attacks.evidence: "writes JPEG at 480/800/1200 px and AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px" ABSENT: a rule that skips or clamps widths above the source or crop width.

attacks.claim: No EXIF orientation (autorotate) step is specified before metadata is stripped. Rotated phone photos can produce sideways derivatives, and crop and focal-point coordinates may be defined on the displayed orientation rather than raw pixels.
attacks.evidence: "colour is converted to sRGB, then all metadata is stripped (`strip=True`)" ABSENT: any orientation-correction step.

attacks.claim: The plan does not order the flag against the writes. If has_responsive_set is set before all keys are uploaded and verified, or a retry leaves a partial set, the template emits source URLs that 404 for real readers.
attacks.evidence: "`<picture>` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task)." ABSENT: flag set only after every key is written and verified, and cleanup of partial sets on retry.

attacks.claim: A legal takedown can be undone. A make_responsive_set job queued or running at purge time, or a backfill run holding the original, can write new AVIF/WebP/JPEG keys after purge_image deletes the prefix. Invalidation completion is also not awaited, and has_responsive_set is not said to be cleared on purge.
attacks.evidence: "It is extended to delete every key under the image's `<id>-` prefix and invalidate `/media/YYYY/MM/<id>-*`." ABSENT: cancellation of queued tasks for that image id, a post-purge prefix re-check, waiting for invalidation completion, or resetting has_responsive_set.

attacks.claim: The backfill has no slack. 310,000 × 0.9 s ÷ 8 workers ≈ 9.7 h against a 10 h window (two 5 h nights). The 0.9 s figure is from a c6i.xlarge prototype, not production nodes, and it is unclear whether it is per worker or per node. Any retry, slowdown, or interrupted night pushes work past the window with no overflow, resume, or progress-alert plan.
attacks.evidence: "0.9 s per image for the full set (prototype, c6i.xlarge). Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00)" ABSENT: production-node throughput measurement, overflow plan, backfill progress metrics or completion alert.

attacks.claim: The claim that publishing is never delayed is unsupported. The backfill runs on the same two nodes as publishing with no dedicated pool, CPU or memory caps, or concurrency limit. No time limit is set for libvips calls, so a hung or OOM-killed decode can hold a slot indefinitely.
attacks.evidence: "on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed." ABSENT: dedicated worker processes or CPU/memory limits, Celery soft/hard time limits for make_responsive_set, and a publish-latency measure during the backfill window.

attacks.claim: Licence coverage for new sizes, formats, and stored copies of wire images, across about 310,000 backfilled images, rests on an informal photo-desk confirmation. Wire licences often restrict alteration and copy creation, and no legal review of the licence terms is shown before the backfill runs.
attacks.evidence: "Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19)." ABSENT: citation to licence clauses or written legal sign-off.

attacks.claim: Inputs are treated as trusted because they come from authenticated staff, but wire and third-party bytes pass through the same path. The plan does not say how file type is verified (magic bytes or extension), and HEIC decoding of attacker-controlled bytes in libvips 8.14 is not isolated. The claim that VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED protects decoding is not tested.
attacks.evidence: "Uploads come only from authenticated CMS staff, and the existing upload validation (JPEG/PNG/WebP/HEIC only, 40-megapixel limit) runs before either task." ABSENT: type-verification method, decoder isolation for HEIC, and a test that VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED is active on the pinned build.

attacks.claim: The purge command has no stated operator authorization or audit record, even though it performs irreversible deletion for legal takedowns.
attacks.evidence: "Kill notices and legal takedowns use the `purge_image` management command" ABSENT: operator authorization check and audit log entry.

attacks.claim: The success target is not yet supported by the plan's own evidence. The prototype reaches 2.6 s, above the 2.5 s goal, and the plan gives no decision rule if production lands above 2.5 s.
attacks.evidence: "p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s" vs "CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%" ABSENT: fallback or decision rule.

attacks.claim: The headline LCP improvement rests on 50 articles on one device profile, and the selection method is not described, so representativeness of the 310,000-article backfill population is unshown.
attacks.evidence: "Prototype (WEB-771) on 50 recent articles" ABSENT: sampling method and comparison to the backfill population.

attacks.claim: The ~9 TB and ~$1,000/month CloudFront savings are labelled an estimate, but the derivation from the prototype byte savings to the traffic mix is not shown.
attacks.evidence: "projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less. This is an estimate" ABSENT: calculation shown.

attacks.claim: The 340 KB per-image figure does not follow from the listed outputs. Eleven derivatives (JPEG at three widths plus AVIF and WebP at four widths each) are not summed, and the prototype reports only 800 px AVIF and WebP medians. Storage cost may be understated, though likely not materially.
attacks.evidence: "~340 KB of new derivatives per image → ~105 GB for the backfill" vs "800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB"

attacks.claim: width and height are taken from 'stored dimensions', which could be the original upload rather than the cropped JPEG that src points to. That would reserve the wrong aspect ratio and cause the layout shift the CLS target guards against.
attacks.evidence: "gains `width`/`height` from stored dimensions to prevent layout shift"

attacks.claim: No visual quality check is specified for AVIF q50 and WebP q75 on news photography. Reader-visible artifacts could ship unnoticed, and the photo desk was consulted only on licensing.
attacks.evidence: "AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px" ABSENT: visual comparison or sign-off step.

attacks.claim: The plan does not state the access policy or metadata handling for the original upload, which can carry GPS data and is deleted by purge_image. Metadata stripping applies only to the derivatives.
attacks.evidence: "all metadata is stripped (`strip=True`)" and purge deletes "the original" ABSENT: original-object access control and metadata policy.

attacks.claim: Stripping all IPTC and XMP from new derivatives can remove copyright and credit fields that licences or attribution may require to travel with the image.
attacks.evidence: "assert none of it survives in any output."

attacks.claim: IAM scope for the new worker role, the purge role, and whether the backfill queue shares credentials with publishing tasks is not specified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: IAM policy for worker, purge, and invalidation rights, and credential separation for the new queue.

attacks.claim: pyvips is a separate Python package with no stated pin, hash, or update procedure, so the binding that parses untrusted bytes is not covered by the stated Debian patch process.
attacks.evidence: "Library: pyvips 2.2 (MIT) on libvips 8.14 from the Debian 12 package ... security updates via unattended-upgrades" ABSENT: pyvips pinning and update procedure.

attacks.claim: No backpressure or priority rule for make_responsive_set during upload bursts. Burst work can queue ahead of the backfill on the same nodes.
attacks.evidence: "New task `make_responsive_set` is queued after it succeeds." ABSENT: queue depth limit or priority rules.

attacks.claim: The has_responsive_set gate is specified only for the article template. Listing and front pages with many images could issue one lookup per image unless prefetched.
attacks.evidence: "`<picture>` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true" ABSENT: query or prefetch strategy for listings.

attacks.claim: Splitting each image into up to 11 objects may lower per-object CDN hit rate and raise origin fetches for the long tail. The claim that hit rate is unaffected addresses only Accept-header negotiation, not object fan-out.
attacks.evidence: "so CloudFront cache keys and hit rate are unaffected" ABSENT: projected per-object hit rate and origin-request measurement.

attacks.claim: The format and width matrix is hard-coded across the task, template, and sizes attribute with no single source of truth, and the mapping of source srcsets to widths is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "`sizes="(max-width: 720px) 100vw, 720px"`" and JPEG 480/800/1200 px versus AVIF and WebP 480/800/1200/1600 px

attacks.claim: Crop and focal-point handling is duplicated between make_display_jpeg and make_responsive_set, with no stated shared code path, so the two can drift.
attacks.evidence: "using the crop rectangle and focal point editors already set" alongside "`make_display_jpeg` ... stays exactly as it is."

attacks.claim: Monitoring omits CloudFront and S3 5xx errors, queue depth or lag, and any has_responsive_set coverage metric. Exhausted-retry images stay silently on plain img.
attacks.evidence: "Monitoring: RUM p75 LCP/CLS per group; CloudFront 4xx rate on `*.avif` / `*.webp`; `make_responsive_set` failures" ABSENT: 5xx alert, queue-lag alert, coverage metric.

attacks.claim: Idempotency is a check-then-write on has_responsive_set with no lock or atomic flag, so a backfill job and a new-upload task can process the same image concurrently.
attacks.evidence: "Idempotent: images with `has_responsive_set` already true are skipped; restarting is safe."

attacks.claim: Bulk cleanup of roughly 310,000 derivative sets is not specified. The only deletion tooling named is the per-image takedown command.
attacks.evidence: "Derivatives can stay in S3 or be deleted by prefix later"
